findings.problem: Toast uses `cubic-bezier(0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94)` (ease-out-quad) for entrance only — there is no exit animation. When dismissed the toast vanishes. This is the most common amateur tell in feedback systems because users register the disappearance subliminally as a glitch.
findings.fix: Refactor toast lifecycle in shell.jsx or wherever toasts are removed. Add: `.toast.leaving { animation: toastOut 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1) forwards; } @keyframes toastOut { from { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } to { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(6px) scale(.98); } }`. In the removal code, add the class first, then `setTimeout(remove, 180)`. Also add `animation-fill-mode: both` to line 909 so the initial keyframe holds.

findings.where: dr-04 mobile: command-strip, live-strip, signal cards
findings.problem: On the mobile collapse (line 829–844) every multi-column grid drops to single column with no entrance reflow. The four command-strip tiles stack into a 4-card tower and all four animate as one block via `.page` fade. On a phone the perceived weight of the page is dominated by the KPI stack, and the lack of per-tile entry makes the scroll feel "dumped on the screen". Also the live-strip on mobile (line 831) collapses to 1fr but contents (clock, House, Senate, Hansard, YouTube, Watch live) reflow with no spacing rhythm visible in dr-04.
findings.fix: Add mobile-specific stagger override: `@media (max-width: 780px) { .command-strip > .panel { animation: ppRise 320ms var(--ease-entrance) both; } .command-strip > .panel:nth-child(1){animation-delay:0ms} .command-strip > .panel:nth-child(2){animation-delay:70ms} .command-strip > .panel:nth-child(3){animation-delay:140ms} .command-strip > .panel:nth-child(4){animation-delay:210ms} .live-strip > * { animation: ppRise 300ms var(--ease-entrance) both; } .live-strip > *:nth-child(n) { animation-delay: calc(60ms * var(--i,0)); } }`. Also tighten mobile `.command-strip` gap from 14px to 10px and `.panel-body` padding from 14px to 12px so the tower compresses ~40px and the user sees the priority panel above the fold.

findings.where: index.html line 367–382 buttons, line 932–938 `:active` block
findings.problem: `.btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); filter: brightness(0.93); }` is a serviceable press state but there is no hover lift, no shadow change, no scale, and the primary button (the most important CTA — "Generate daily brief" and "Watch live") only changes box-shadow on hover. The primary ember button is the single brand object on the page and it gets no character on hover beyond a glow. Compare Linear or Stripe where primary buttons subtly scale and shift gradient angle.
findings.fix: Replace lines 374–379 with: `.btn { transition: background 140ms var(--ease-functional), border-color 140ms var(--ease-functional), box-shadow 180ms var(--ease-functional), transform 120ms var(--ease-functional), filter 120ms var(--ease-functional); } .btn:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); } .btn.primary { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #f5934a, #e07d33); transition: background 180ms var(--ease-functional), box-shadow 180ms var(--ease-functional), transform 120ms var(--ease-functional); } .btn.primary:hover { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #f89e58, #e5853a); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(240,138,60,.6), 0 4px 14px -2px rgba(255,157,79,.5), 0 0 18px -4px var(--brass-2); transform: translateY(-1px); }`. The translateY(-1) on hover plus translateY(+1) on active gives the 2px tactile arc that reads as quality.

findings.where: index.html line 199 sidebar light-theme `.nav-item.active` and lines 287–295 active indicator
findings.problem: The ember left-border on the active nav item appears statically. There is no transition when navigating between sidebar items — the indicator jumps. Linear, Vercel, Notion all animate the indicator between items with a shared-element move. Here, switching from Overview to All signals snaps.
findings.fix: Lift the indicator to a single element animated between items. Add `<span class="nav-pointer" />` as a sibling of the nav list in shell.jsx, position absolute relative to `.nav`, with `top` and `height` tweened via `transition: transform 280ms var(--ease-entrance), height 240ms var(--ease-entrance);`. On click of any `.nav-item`, set the pointer's `top` and `height` to match the clicked item's `getBoundingClientRect()`. Remove the `::before` pseudo-element pattern at line 291–295 so only the shared pointer renders. Fallback: if state is reorganisation-heavy, keep the per-item `::before` but transition it from `width: 0` to `width: 3px` via `transition: width 240ms var(--ease-entrance);` so it grows in on activation.

findings.where: index.html line 728–730 `.page` fade vs line 850 `.modal-back` fade — duplicate fadeIn
findings.problem: Two different elements share `@keyframes fadeIn` but apply it with different durations and easings (`var(--dur-page)` vs `.18s ease-out-quad`). This is fine but reveals that the motion language is being declared inconsistently — the modal does not use the design-system `--ease-entrance` token. The token vocabulary is correct, the application is sloppy.
findings.fix: Replace line 850 `animation: fadeIn .18s cubic-bezier(0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94);` with `animation: fadeIn 200ms var(--ease-functional);`. Audit every animation declaration in index.html — every duration must be `var(--dur-micro|--dur|--dur-page)`, every easing must be one of the three motion tokens. Add a comment block at the top of the motion-tokens section enforcing this. The lint rule should flag any inline `cubic-bezier(` outside `:root`.

findings.where: index.html line 733–743 `.skeleton` and any loading state
findings.problem: Skeleton uses a 2.4s linear shimmer — correct duration choice. But the shimmer band is white-tinted (`#ffffff22`) on dark, and there is no light-theme override, so on warm paper it would shimmer with a hot-white band that breaks the cream palette. Mobile loading would betray the brand.
findings.fix: Add to the light theme block (around line 200): `[data-theme="light"] .skeleton { background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--panel) 0%, rgba(80,50,20,.06) 40%, rgba(80,50,20,.10) 50%, rgba(80,50,20,.06) 60%, var(--panel) 100%); background-size: 200% 100%; }`. Also slow to 2.8s on light for the warm-paper register feel.

findings.where: index.html line 745–748 focus-visible
findings.problem: Focus ring is a hard 2px solid ember outline with 2px offset — correct accessibility but visually clunky on a refined product. No transition on appearance, no soft glow.
findings.fix: Update line 747: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--brass); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--accent-ring); transition: box-shadow 120ms var(--ease-functional), outline-color 120ms var(--ease-functional); }`. The added box-shadow halo softens the ring into the ember accent-ring token and matches the search-bar focus halo pattern at line 339.

findings.where: index.html line 894–901 `.live-strip` `stripPulse` animation
findings.problem: The live-strip left-border pulses between `var(--ember-flash)` and a 45%-alpha version — a blinking strip is restless and pulls attention away from the actual signal cards. Two competing pulses on the same page (live-badge dot + live-strip border) compete for the user's focal point. This is the classic "too many things move" amateur tell.
findings.fix: Remove the `stripPulse` animation on `.live-strip` entirely (delete lines 899–901). Keep the static `border-left: 3px solid var(--ember-flash)`. The ember spine should be a declared identity, not a flashing alert. Reserve the breathing pulse for the LIVE badge dot only — one pulse on the page at a time.

critiques.lens: First-time senior policy executive opening a public parliamentary-intelligence product in dark, light, drawer and mobile views.
critiques.verdict: It reads as a polished personal hobby dashboard, not a credible commercial product, because the screen drowns the reader in two oversized warning banners and four equal-weight ember KPIs before any actual signal is visible, and the light theme ships with a visible theme bug that no professional team would let out the door.

findings.where: dr-02-overview-light.jpeg, first KPI tile 'New signals today'
findings.problem: The hero KPI card renders with the dark-theme panel gradient on warm-paper light mode, producing a black rectangle on cream paper. This is the single most damaging tell: a visible theme bug on the marketing screenshot says 'unfinished'.
findings.fix: In index.html the .cs-primary rule (line 408-418) hardcodes radial gradient #f08a3c14 over var(--panel-2). Add a [data-theme='light'] .cs-primary override: background: radial-gradient(420px 140px at 0% 0%, rgba(154,82,25,0.06), transparent), linear-gradient(180deg, var(--panel) 0%, var(--panel-2) 100%); border-color: var(--line-2). Same fix for any .panel.stat.hero-stat used by PageOverview at pages.jsx line 137 (currently uses inline borderLeft and inherits panel gradient which works, but verify against [data-theme='light'] .panel rule — there is no light override for .panel, only for .signal at index.html line 167).

findings.where: dr-01 and dr-02 top of overview, both banners
findings.problem: Two stacked yellow-orange disclaimer banners ('Design state' + 'Representative data') plus a third 'Getting started' panel consume the entire above-the-fold band. A senior reader sees three warning-coloured bars before any content. It screams beta/demo/personal-project, not product.
findings.fix: Collapse the two data-warning banners into ONE compact line directly under the topbar, height 28px, mono 11px, ink-3 colour, no border, single icon. Move 'Getting started' out of the main column entirely into a dismissable side-rail or a '?' help popover triggered from the topbar. In pages.jsx PageOverview (lines 117-122) delete the .design-banner block and remove <OnboardingGuide />; add one new <div className='meta-strip'> with the disclaimer text. Add to index.html: .meta-strip { display:flex; gap:12px; padding:6px 16px; font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; color:var(--ink-4); border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); }.

findings.where: dr-01, dr-02, dr-04 — the four-tile KPI strip
findings.problem: All four KPI numbers (6, 3, 7, 6) read at near-identical visual weight despite the design system declaring 't-kpi 48px' for the hero and 't-stat 28px' for the rest. The intended hero-vs-secondary contrast is not landing because the hero number '6' is the same digit count as the rest and the cards are roughly the same width (1.6fr vs 1fr is too close). Result: a row of indistinct dashboard tiles, the visual cliche of every amateur SaaS demo.
findings.fix: Change .command-strip grid in index.html line 405 from '1.6fr 1fr 1fr 1fr' to '2.4fr 1fr 1fr 1fr'. In pages.jsx line 137 add an additional element to the hero card: a sparkline or a 7-day delta bar (use an SVG, fill var(--brass) at 0.6 opacity) sitting below the KPI value. Drop --t-stat from 28px to 22px in :root (line 101) so the secondary numbers visibly recede. Add font-weight:700 to .cs-primary .cs-kpi but keep font-weight:500 on .cs-secondary .cs-stat. The three secondary tiles should also lose their card chrome (border, gradient, shadow) and become flat label/number stacks separated only by a 1px var(--line) vertical divider, like a Bloomberg masthead.

findings.where: dr-01, dr-02, dr-03 — every 'Fixture' chip on every signal card and KPI label
findings.problem: The ALL-CAPS letter-spacing .18em mono labels appear on the brand subtitle, every panel kicker, every stat label, every section header, every fixture chip, every group of nav. The screen has dozens of identical-looking mono-uppercase tags. The signal that was meant to be a chrome detail has become the dominant texture, making the page look like a 2014 admin template rather than a 2026 product.
findings.fix: Audit and cut. In index.html: remove text-transform:uppercase from .panel-kicker (line 472), .stat-label (line 480), and .chip-fixture (line 965) — keep it ONLY on .nav-group (line 274) and .page-kicker (line 397). Drop letter-spacing across the board from .18em to .08em. Change .chip-fixture from uppercase 'FIXTURE' to sentence-case italic serif 'fixture' in var(--ink-4) with no border, no background — let it sit inline as low-weight metadata, not as a pill. This single change will roughly halve the visual noise.

findings.where: dr-01, dr-03 — every signal card body, recommended-action row and the 5-bar attention glyph in lower-right of each card
findings.problem: The recommended-action ('Assign Policy Owner', 'Draft Executive Brief') is rendered with the same weight and treatment as the body summary above it, and the cute orange 5-bar 'attention meter' in the card corner is decorative cruft that adds nothing a number could not. A serious product surfaces the recommended decision FIRST and removes ornament.
findings.fix: Restructure SignalCard in pages.jsx so the recommended action becomes a coloured strip at the top of the card with the verb ('Assign Policy Owner') as 15px ink-on-brass-soft pill, followed by the title, followed by a single-line summary clamp at 1.5em. Delete the 5-bar attention SVG entirely (it duplicates the HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW tag at the top). Replace with a single small numeric '4/5' in mono ink-4 next to the source. In index.html add: .signal { display:grid; grid-template-areas: 'action action' 'meta meta' 'title title' 'summary summary' 'tags tags'; gap:8px; }, then move the 'RECOMMENDED' row into the .action grid area at the top.

findings.where: dr-01 sidebar 'Active 2 days this week' under Juan Vega, and the dr-03 drawer top-right '1 / 6 SIGNAL' badge with orange box
findings.problem: Personal name and activity streak in a public-facing parliamentary intelligence product reads as a single-user toy, not a product. The '1/6 SIGNAL' orange-bordered widget in the drawer header is meaningless to a first-time reader and visually competes with the close button.
findings.fix: Either remove the user profile chip from the public marketing screens entirely, or replace 'Juan Vega / Principal Policy Officer / Active 2 days this week' with the organisation mark ('Prometheus Policy Lab' / 'Tier: Pro / Sign in'). The orange-bordered 1/6 chip in the drawer needs to be demoted: change to ink-4 mono '1 of 6', no border, sitting beside the close button in the same row, not as a separate badge.

findings.where: dr-04 mobile overview
findings.problem: Mobile collapses to a single column but the four KPI tiles stack into a 4-deep block of full-width cards before the user reaches any signal. Combined with the two banners, the user must scroll past five hero-card-height blocks before seeing one signal. Mobile feels like a desktop dashboard squashed, not designed.
findings.fix: On viewports under 720px, in index.html @media block near line 831, collapse the KPI strip to a 2x2 grid (grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr) and halve the padding to 10px 12px. Move the hero KPI to a single full-width row above the 2x2. Also force the 'Getting started' onboarding card to collapse to a single-line link 'How this works ->' under the page title.

findings.where: dr-03 drawer — the green horizontal bars on 'Attention score breakdown'
findings.problem: The bars use saturated mint-green that does not appear anywhere else in the product palette. The design system explicitly says (index.html line 60-66) the only sanctioned greens fold into teal-verified family at #45b3a4 and no standalone green exists, but the rendered bars look brighter and more saturated than the declared --teal. Looks like a stock Chart.js default leaked through.
findings.fix: Audit the score-bar component in pages.jsx (SignalDrawer); replace whatever inline colour it uses with background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--brass-soft) 0%, var(--brass) 100%) so the breakdown bars match the ember sovereign accent system. Bars should be 4px tall not 6px, and aligned with the right-edge number column. If teal is preferred for 'verification' semantics, use exactly var(--teal) with no saturation boost.

findings.where: dr-01, dr-02 — page title 'Today's signals' and its sub-line
findings.problem: The serif H1 'Today's signals' at 30px sits flat with no kicker prominence, and the sub-line 'representative signal items / classified as priority / official feeds configured' repeats numbers already shown in the KPI strip 100px below. Redundancy and weak masthead.
findings.fix: Raise --t-masthead from 30px to 36px in :root (line 96). Replace the sub-line with a one-sentence editorial standfirst in 16px serif italic ink-2 that explains the value of the page ('Sitting day 1 June. Six new items since yesterday, three need a decision before House sitting at 9am'). Move the numeric breakdown to mono micro-labels under the KPIs, not under the title.

findings.where: dr-01 — the orange 'Watch live' button beside Hansard/YouTube ghost buttons in the live-strip row
findings.problem: The live-strip has three CTAs of nearly equal prominence (Hansard, YouTube, Watch live) plus a 'Generate daily brief' primary button up top right plus a 'New brief' primary button in the topbar. Four ember-primary buttons compete on one screen. The design CSS comment at line 39-47 explicitly says primary ember is one per surface; the implementation breaks its own rule.
findings.fix: Enforce one-primary-per-surface. In pages.jsx PageOverview: the only .btn.primary should be 'Generate daily brief' in page-head. Demote 'Watch live' (line 181) to .btn.ghost with a left ember dot indicator. Demote topbar 'New brief' (in app.jsx) to .btn.sm.ghost with an ember outline. Demote 'Refresh live' similarly. Result: one ember button, every other action is ghost or outline, ember reads as sovereign again.

findings.where: dr-01, dr-02 — entire signal-card grid spacing and the right-rail 'What changed / Briefing queue / Source health'
findings.problem: Vertical rhythm is broken. Gaps between banners, KPI strip, live strip, panel header, and signal cards vary between 12px and 22px with no consistent baseline. The right rail panels (What changed, Briefing queue, Source health) stack with three different border styles and the 'Source health' table has empty dash columns that read as 'we have not finished this'.
findings.fix: Set --sp-row: 16px and use it uniformly between every top-level block. Remove the empty dash columns from Source health table (the four feeds with '—' columns) — show only Status + Last-poll, and only show one column 'Last poll: 5 min ago' in mono ink-3. If polling data is not available yet, hide the table behind a 'Source health — coming soon' kicker rather than show empty placeholder rows. Right-rail panels should share one panel chrome rule; remove inline overrides.

findings.where: All four screens — the brand-mark glow on the dark Parliament Pulse logo top-left
findings.problem: The brand mark is a soft orange radial glow with no actual logomark inside it, just an empty round-rect. On a public product the empty glow reads as a placeholder a designer forgot to fill in. The BETA pill next to 'Parliament Pulse' compounds the placeholder feel.
findings.fix: Put an actual mark inside .brand-mark (index.html line 259) — either a stylised P, a flame glyph from the Fire House identity, or the Prometheus Lab triangle. SVG, 24x24, currentColor=var(--brass). Drop the BETA pill from the public screen (the 'Design state' banner already communicates pre-release). Keep the radial glow but tighten it: reduce brand-mark size from 52px to 40px so the brand block is denser.
